title: brain: theOS's memory, one schema, references pinned by commit
note: brain: the schema, the reflection and the trace of everything theOS keeps. It took AIP-1's memory parts (D-25).

questions.q: Is brain's direction right: a JSON doc per thing, JSON Lines for whatever only grows, a JSON Schema per type, binaries named by content hash, and every internal reference pinned as path@full commit SHA?

source.text: lets talk about our schema format of SSOT for all related data that we generate on AIPs and learnings and resources etc ... what is a json file or list of json entries, what is markdown or what is both? ... also any kind of our internal git resource should be linked universally via its committed commit hashes, never via just a file path, since history changes too

who: Samuel Andert, who must trust that the agents follow what he decided, as it stands now.
avenMAIA and its agents, which read brain before they act and write to it as they work.
Anyone who later asks why something is the way it is.
problem.experience: Decisions, words and history were kept in chat and in files edited in place: a newer decision did not say what it replaced, outdated words came back, and nobody could tell which step wrote what.

items.text: Decisions were listed oldest first, and a newer one did not say which older one it replaced (the dated decision docs, before D-15).
avenCEO had to be renamed by hand across 13 types, 25 terms and three apps, twice (D-17, D-21).
A read flag on 58 sources claimed a global truth that was per intent (D-22).
A link is a bare path, and the file behind it changes (D-12).

problem.baseline: Now: 26 decisions, 35 terms and 3 intents, one JSON doc each in theOS/; the reflection and the trace computed by the apps; no schema, no check that history only grows, links by bare path.
whys: You can't be sure the agents follow what holds now. Why? Old and new decisions sat side by side, edited in place, without saying which replaces which.
Why? Memory had no rules: no schema per type, no history that only grows, no reflection, links that move.
Root cause: brain has no schema, and nothing enforces the reflection, the trace or the growth of history.
truths: Git keeps every version of every file; a commit SHA names exactly one.
What is computed from a log that only grows cannot drift from it.
A JSON Schema is checked by a program, without judgement.
Whether a new decision replaces an old one needs judgement: an agent proposes it, the decision records it.
assumptions: One JSON doc per thing stays fast enough for the apps at a few hundred docs.
Rewriting git history stays forbidden, so a pinned commit never disappears.
problem.risk: Medium: it changes how every doc is written, not what ships.

options.name: The direction you approved (D-25)
options.note: A JSON doc per thing, JSON Lines for what only grows, a JSON Schema per type, internal references pinned as path@full commit SHA; binaries by content hash when there are any.

options.name: A database
options.note: Rejected: git already versions, diffs and reviews files; a database would need its own history and review.

claims.promise: Every doc in theOS/ matches its type's JSON Schema, in theOS's check.
claims.fails: A misspelt field or a missing author passes unseen.
claims.check: Each schema rejects a planted bad doc of its type; every current doc passes.

claims.promise: What only grows (an intent's events, a metric's measurements, a session's asks) lives in JSON Lines, and a change that edits or drops an earlier line fails.
claims.fails: History is rewritten and nothing notices.
claims.check: The check requires the base commit's file to be a prefix of the new one; a planted edit of an old line fails.

claims.promise: No decision or term is committed without its reflection, and every supersedes points at a doc that exists; what holds is only ever computed.
claims.fails: A decision lands without saying what it replaces, or points at nothing.
claims.check: The check fails a planted decision without reflection, and one whose supersedes names a missing doc.

claims.promise: Every doc is written by an event of an intent, by an author doc.
claims.fails: A doc appears that no step wrote, or an author is a free string.
claims.check: The check fails a planted doc that no event writes, and an event whose by is not an author doc; docs from before brain are covered by one back-fill event each.

claims.promise: An internal reference is pinned as path@full commit SHA when it is written, and the apps show the pinned version and flag a target changed since.
claims.fails: A link silently shows content that changed after it was cited.
claims.check: A planted pin to an older commit of a doc that changed since is flagged in the apps.

outcome.promise: Over the next three sessions: no correction caused by an outdated decision or word coming back.
outcome.how: Each correction is an event by Samuel Andert (what: correction); counted per session.

checkpoints.adds: A JSON Schema per type in theOS/aven/types/, checked by theOS's check over every doc.
Events, measurements and asks moved to JSON Lines; the growth check.
The reflection and the trace enforced by the check.
References pinned by commit, and the apps' flag.

deferred.what: The reflection run by a fresh checker, automatically
deferred.until: It has run by hand three times without a miss.
